clinician.final_diagnosis: ALK+ histiocytosis with pathological features of juvenile xanthogranulomatosis (JXG).
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 2-month-old male infant presented with worsening tachypnoea and a rapidly enlarging skin lesion. Biopsy of skin and pulmonary lesions revealed a highly proliferative histiocytosis, positive for ALK, CD33, and factor XIIIa, weakly positive for CD68, and negative for CD1a and Langerin. Whole body MRI and PET/CT imaging confirmed extensive systemic involvement including pulmonary, spinal cord, brain, and lymph node lesions. Molecular testing further identified a translocated KIF5B-ALK fusion rearrangement.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation included worsening tachypnoea and a rapidly enlarging, smooth-topped, infiltrative, bronze-yellow nodule with overlying telangiectasias on the mid-sternum.
Biopsy of skin and pulmonary lesions demonstrated a highly proliferative histiocytosis.
Immunohistochemical staining showed positive immunoreactivity for ALK, CD33, and factor XIIIa, and weak positivity for CD68.
Immunohistochemical staining was negative for CD1a and Langerin.

Whole body MRI and PET/CT imaging confirmed extensive systemic involvement including pulmonary, compressing spinal cord lesions, a metabolically active right meningeal/parietal parenchymal brain tumour, and extensive mediastinal/abdominal lymphadenopathy.
Molecular testing (FISH and DNA sequencing) revealed a translocated KIF5B-ALK fusion rearrangement.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Immunohistochemical staining was negative for CD1a and Langerin (E002), which are markers for LCH.

remaining_uncertainties: Detailed morphological histopathological description of juvenile xanthogranulomatosis features beyond immunohistochemistry.
Patient's response to treatment and long-term outcome.
